subject.title: refactor: remove expired plugin compatibility surfaces

question: Should the July 21, 2026 release deliberately remove plugin SDK contracts whose registry removal windows run through July 24–30, 2026?
rationale: The registry timing is an externally visible upgrade contract, and accepting an early cutover is a release-policy choice rather than a mechanical refactor decision.

options.title: Honor the recorded removal windows
options.body: Retain every contract until its individual removeAfter date and merge only the removals already eligible on the release date.

options.title: Explicitly approve an early compatibility cut
options.body: Proceed before the published dates only with an explicit release-policy decision, prominent migration communication, and acceptance of external-plugin breakage.

options.title: Pause the compatibility sweep
options.body: Defer the broad removal PR until the relevant registry windows have elapsed and the remaining migration evidence is simpler to verify.

recommendation.title: Honor the recorded removal windows
recommendation.body: Retain every contract until its individual removeAfter date and merge only the removals already eligible on the release date.

likelyOwner.reason: The branch history and self-assignment connect steipete most directly to the sweep and its intended release timing, though current-main ownership was not independently established.
